title: Cats May Meow to Ask Us to Solve Their Problems
paragraphs: Your cat has a problem — so, naturally, it's your problem too!
Maybe they're trying to tell you they're hungry, or that they want to play. But they won't stop meowing until you solve the problem.
And a new study suggests that this meowing may really be a cat's way of asking for help. It found that cats are more than four times as likely to meow when humans are around!
The study was done by researchers in Brazil, and included 38 pet cats. The owners said their cats meowed a lot around food.
So each cat had their favorite treat put inside a small plastic box that had holes in it. Although they could smell the treat, they could not open the box.
The researchers then observed the cats for one minute under two different conditions: alone, and with a person in the room.
The cats meowed 86 times when a human was in the room, compared with 20 meows when the cats were alone.
The researchers also noticed that, when a person was in the room, the cats looked at them a lot — sometimes looking from the person to the treat box.
When the cats were alone, they mostly stood still and looked at the door.
The results suggest that, when faced with a problem they couldn't solve, the cats were more likely to meow if a human was around to help.

However, the researchers said this study could not confirm that every meow was a deliberate request. The study was also quite small, and was done with cats that were already known to meow around food.
But the next time you hear a cat meow, it might be trying to tell you something!
